newsitem.title: FRANCE: French carmakers to show jointly made transmission.
newsitem.headline: French carmakers to show jointly made transmission.

text.p: French carmakers PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault SA are preparing to unveil an automatic transmission that they developed jointly as part of a drive to cut production costs.
"In a few days we will present a new transmission which will be produced at both Renault and Peugeot sites," PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Wednesday.

The transmission, scheduled to be shown on July 1, is the second component developed jointly by the two companies. They developed a V6 engine in 1971 and invested 1.3 billion francs last year to make a new V6 engine for their larger cars.
The V6 is made by Francaise de Mecanique, a 50-50 venture formed by the two car companies in 1969, three years after their respective chairmen signed the first joint production agreement.
PSA and Renault, which face falling sales in their home market and high costs associated with their comparatively small size, both resist suggestions from politicians that they should merge.
There is too much overlap in their products and the result would be a smaller French car industry and tens of thousands of job losses, Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer has said.
The way of the future, they say, is more cooperative agreements on components like the V6 and the new transmission.
"On marginal cars -- but not at the heart of our model range -- we are not hostile to cooperation," Calvet told the annual general meeting.
The PSA group produces multi-purpose vehicles and light commercial vehicles at the Sevelnord plant in northern France with Fiat for the Citroen, Peugeot, Fiat and Lancia brands.
Renault has an agreement with General Motors Corp to develop and sell light commercial vehicles in Europe and is trying to negotiate an accord to build motors with Germany's MAN.
